lead: Tesla / TSLA - the Musk dip the crowd won't sell
smaller: Ripple / XRP - the SEC fight is over
Robinhood / HOOD - bet on the Fed like a ballgame
Quantum computing / IONQ - the next computing revolution
why_lead: Tesla closed at 278.39 after an 11.93% prior-session jump and a 16.97% five-session rally, still 15.77% below its 20-session reference of 330.53, which is the price evidence that a sharp drawdown is being bought. The attention evidence is explicit in the dated reporting: Forbes on Musk's 'hang on', Reuters on tariff leeway and a lower share price drawing investors, and Fortune on Nvidia overtaking Tesla as the most-held stock on Robinhood.

The simple story the crowd repeats is that a Musk-run stock is a discount on every drop, and the same names recur across the attention pieces. The institutional view is split on direction rather than pace, so the trade is a live argument rather than a settled one.
Every citation rests on prices and headlines dated before 00:00 UTC on 2025-03-25; no later outcome is used to choose the lead.
why_smaller: Ripple / XRP: the SEC-case rally is the retail story, and the spike has already faded back to the 20-session reference of 2.46 while flows rotate toward XRP and Solana ETPs.
Robinhood / HOOD: a non-AI, platform-level trade with a clear prediction-markets story, a 9.02% prior-session move and a Massachusetts regulatory probe already in the reporting.

Quantum computing / IONQ: the same drawdown-and-bounce shape as Tesla but a different narrative (Big Tech race, insider buying, CEO caution), with a 17.34% prior-session jump against a 16.39% 20-session decline.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir (PLTR): +10.76% over five sessions and +6.69% over 20, with analyst-favourite pieces, but no single move or dated catalyst that the crowd is buying; the Tesla drawdown-and-bounce is the sharper set-up.
Bitcoin and ether: flat to lower over 20 sessions (BTC +0.32%, ETH -4.26%); the crowd's bitcoin items are forecasts rather than a surge, so crypto is covered in the crypto block instead.
Gold (GLD): record-high headlines, but GLD is down 0.45% in the prior session; the miners are the cheaper and under-owned expression, so they went to the underowned themes.
Rocket Lab (RKLB): a 40% crash headline without a clear crowd-buying story in the window.
Nebius (NBIS): +8.19% in the prior session against -19.41% over 20, with no trending-attention item in this day's reporting that carries the story.
Oklo (OKLO): strong moves on company releases (NRC readiness, board changes), but thin crowd evidence beyond the company's own news.
Trump Media (DJT): the Crypto.com ETF deal is a single-day news item rather than a sustained retail trade.
Micron and Nvidia: large-cap moves on earnings and the GTC keynote; they fail the surge test on size and are covered in sectors and catalysts.
